title: SpecGuard: Inference-Time Backdoor Detection For Free
quote: The per-query AUROC ranges from 0.929 to 0.974, showing strong separation between clean and triggered queries.
proves: Draft-token acceptance rate, scored as a clean-calibrated one-sided deviation, already serves as a runtime detector of target-model behavior shift (backdoors); LLaMA-3B target + 1B draft, Llama3/Gemma3/Qwen3 1B-32B; FPR 0.033-0.097 at TPR 0.95; first 8 evaluated positions give AUROC 0.94; main false positives are naturally low-acceptance short high-entropy queries; recommends pinning and verifying the draft checkpoint; conclusion says spec decode 'already computes a signal about model integrity'.
does_not_prove: Does not study hardware faults, bit flips, SDC, weight corruption, or drafter staleness; backdoor shift is large and trigger-aligned, unlike small numeric faults; no per-device fleet aggregation.
bearing: Same mechanism as C3 (acceptance as integrity signal) and C2 (acceptance-deviation detector): kills novelty of the statistic; leaves the hardware-fault application

title: Revisiting Cauchy-Schwarz Norm Bounds for SDC Detection in LLM Inference
quote: retains 99% of the fault detection capability of ABFT
proves: Cheap norm-bound check (CSNB) for linear layers detects SDC in LLM inference with ~99% of ABFT detection at 87% less verification overhead; only ~55% of ABFT detection for MoE router gates (Oct 2026).
does_not_prove: Does not use a second model or speculative decoding; covers linear layers, not end-to-end output change.
bearing: Strong low-cost baseline C3 must beat; shrinks the cost gap acceptance statistics could exploit

title: Understanding LLM Hallucinations Caused by Soft Errors
quote: performed a case study to understand LLM hallucination caused by soft errors on hardware
proves: LLMEI injects soft errors into LLM inference and builds a taxonomy of hallucination failure modes under different error rates (math, code tasks); Oct 2026.
does_not_prove: Abstract proposes no detector and gives no fraction of outputs changed; no speculative decoding.
bearing: Shows soft-error-induced plausible wrong output is an active topic; scoop risk for C3

title: ESupNNet: An Error Supervising Neural Network architecture for error detection against soft errors in parameters
proves: A separate supervising network watching a protected CNN's class relationships detects single parameter soft errors with over 90% accuracy, without changing the CNN.
does_not_prove: CNN classifiers only; supervisor size and overhead not quantified on the abstract page; no LLMs or generation.
bearing: Adjacent: a second learned model as soft-error detector exists for CNNs; C3's 'free second predictor' is the LLM analogue

title: Silent Data Corruption in AI (OCP whitepaper; NVIDIA, Meta, Google, AMD, Intel, ARM, Microsoft)
quote: a corrupted device results in corruptions across thousands of inference consumers
proves: Industry consensus: inference SDC comes from persistent device defects, hits thousands of consumers per bad device; 'large deviations are easier to detect than smaller deviations, as anomaly detectors can be set up to limit the expected ranges of inference'; triage needs telemetry at each inference sub-stage.
does_not_prove: Gives no inference SDC rate and no output-change frequency; names no speculative-decoding signal.
bearing: Supports C3 relevance (persistent per-device faults suit per-device acceptance aggregation); range anomaly detectors are the baseline

title: Safeguarding LLM Training at Scale: Online SDC Detection and Insights from 35 Million GPU Hours (AEGIS)
quote: In a production deployment spanning 3.5 × 107 GPU-hours, AEGIS identified 18 real-world SDC incidents
proves: ByteDance production: 18 SDC incidents, 13 faulty GPUs in 3.5e7 GPU-hours (about 1 faulty GPU per 2.7M GPU-hours) detected online at 0.86% overhead with a two-stage sensor/verifier design.
does_not_prove: Training, not inference; per-GPU rate and fraction that change outputs not stated on the page.
bearing: Oracle/relevance for C3: real GPU SDC is rare per GPU-hour; a cheap sensor + expensive verifier design already exists

title: Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models
quote: the scale of Gemini means that we can expect SDC events to impact training every week or two
proves: Google saw SDC events every week or two at Gemini training scale and detected them with deterministic replay plus proactive SDC scanners on idle machines and hot standbys.
does_not_prove: Training only; no inference SDC rate.
bearing: Relevance for C3: SDC is routine at fleet scale; baselines are replay and scanners

title: Analysis of LLM Vulnerability to GPU Soft Errors: An Instruction-Level Fault Injection Study (full text)
quote: Floating-point instructions, on the other hand, are more likely to cause SDCs, accounting for 59% of all SDCs.
proves: Extends ledger L106 with numbers: 3000 instruction-level faults per LLM gave exactly 200 SDCs (~6.7%); bit 30 SDC probability up to 23.4%/24.2% (GPT2/Llama3.2), low bits under 1%; lm_head is the most vulnerable operator, LayerNorm least; models include Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B.
does_not_prove: No runtime detector; no speculative decoding; per-model SDC split only in figures.
bearing: Key for C3 combination: lm_head (shared by EAGLE/MTP drafters and target) is the most vulnerable operator, a common-mode path acceptance cannot see

title: Understanding Error Propagation in Deep Learning Neural Network (DNN) Accelerators and Applications
quote: a symptom-based detector that provides 97.84% precision and 92.08% recall in error detection, for selected DNNs and data types
proves: Value-range symptom detectors on activations catch SDC-causing faults with high precision and recall at low cost, because SDC-causing faults produce large value deviations.
does_not_prove: CNN accelerators, 2017; not LLMs or generation.
bearing: The 'logit/activation range check' baseline C3 names; sets a high bar for cheap detection of large faults

title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
quote: the rollout engine re-scores each finished sequence with a prefill pass rather than reporting the log-probabilities its decode kernels produced
proves: True-on-policy mode reaches train-rollout logprob diff exactly zero by batch-invariant matmuls plus rescoring each finished sequence with a prefill pass; profile only dense Qwen3 0.6B/4B; guarantee covers only sampled-token logprob, not the full distribution. Sec 4.4: an opt-in tensor-by-tensor weight check (bit-exact by default, run once at training start, engine prefilled with random values) can target the model, 'the draft model that multi-token prediction adds, or at both'. Miles runs MTP for GLM-5.2 RL.
does_not_prove: Does not say whether true-on-policy mode was run with spec/MTP rollouts; the weight check is opt-in, start-of-training only, and meant for debug runs.
bearing: Kills C1 core (rescoring makes returned logprobs independent of spec); narrows C2 (drafter weight verification exists)

title: IsoExec: Unified Execution to Eliminate Trainer-Inference Mismatch in SkyRL (vLLM blog)
quote: IsoExec eliminates train–inference mismatch with an execution contract and unified model.
proves: Second bitwise train-inference system: execution contract with SHA-256 digests, batch-invariant kernels, deterministic MoE, GDN on one rounding schedule; 25% end-to-end overhead on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (generation +31.3%).
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding or MTP; next steps list Blackwell, CP invariance, sparse attention, block-FP8 MoE.
bearing: C1 scoop risk: active teams; spec omitted again

title: slime train_infer_mismatch_helper README
quote: is recomputed with Megatron at the beginning of each training step
proves: slime recomputes old logprobs on the trainer by default; rollout logprobs are only used with --use-rollout-logprobs; TIS/MIS and rejection sampling correct residual mismatch.
bearing: C1 simplicity: default RL stacks do not consume engine-side logprobs, so spec-returned logprob numerics matter only in opt-in paths

title: Weight Checker (vLLM docs)
quote: Buffers, draft models and LoRA adapters are not checked.
proves: vLLM's SHA-256 per-parameter weight checker (POST /weight_checker, dev mode) verifies RL weight updates on every rank but explicitly excludes draft models; hashing copies weights to CPU.
does_not_prove: Says nothing on why drafters are excluded or on plans to add them.
bearing: C2: the hashing baseline exists for target only; extending it to drafters is engineering

title: Distribute and Update Rollout Weights (NVIDIA Dynamo docs)
quote: The version is caller-supplied metadata, not a tensor digest
proves: Dynamo's weight_version is a caller-set label; docs advise an immutable checkpoint ID or digest and a validation checklist with post-update generation and injected failures; 'the current router does not select workers by that value'.
does_not_prove: No mention of draft, speculative, or MTP models.
bearing: C2: version tags do not prove resident tensors, but the recommended digest practice would catch drafter skew

title: vLLM issues labeled speculative-decoding created 2026-04-20..2026-10-20 (REST list, my classification)
quote: [Bug]: Spec decode hits illegal memory access when the draft model's context is shorter than the target's
proves: Of 74 issues, 24 match crash/hang/assert/corrupt/fail; my split: ~10 fail at startup or warmup (62340, 62028, 59292, 57630, 56917, 56787, 56281, 53612, 53428, 62143), ~7 silently change output with no crash (61115, 58485, 56077, 53505, 53488, 46249, 40875), 4 are runtime illegal memory access (sticky CUDA: 61330, 57941, 56771, 56470), 2 are runtime Python-level exceptions (56419, 55503).
does_not_prove: Title-plus-skim classification by one reader; issue bodies not all read; label coverage incomplete.
bearing: C4 oracle: per-request in-process quarantine applies to about 2 of 74 issues

title: MTP speculative decoding crashes with PP>1 due to missing record_stream on idx_mapping (vLLM #56470)
quote: MTP speculative decoding crashes with `EngineDeadError` / `illegal memory access` when running with pipeline parallelism (PP>1).
proves: A drafter-path stream bug (draft broadcast on last PP rank) corrupts allocator-reused memory and kills the engine with an illegal memory access.
does_not_prove: Single config (TP2 PP3 A100); fixed by record_stream.
bearing: C4: drafter runtime faults are often sticky CUDA errors that no in-process quarantine can contain

title: OffloadingConnector multi-tier + MTP speculative decoding crashes EngineCore in _build_store_jobs (vLLM #55503)
quote: the crash happens the moment a request actually starts producing output.
proves: A Python assert in the KV offload path under MTP kills EngineCore on the first real generation step, after health checks pass.
does_not_prove: Fault is in the offloading connector, not the drafter proper; deterministic on every request, so quarantine would degrade every request to non-spec.
bearing: C4: Python-level spec faults exist but are deterministic; quarantine equals disabling spec

title: Model Runner V2 hangs during speculative decoding warmup with pipeline parallelism (vLLM #62143)
quote: This can be reproduced during GLM-4.7-Flash initialization, before serving any requests.
proves: A spec+PP fault manifests at startup warmup, before any request is in flight.
bearing: C4: startup-time spec faults need no request containment

title: CUDA errors: determine sticky-ness (NVIDIA developer forum)
quote: In the CUDA runtime API, a corrupted CUDA context is non-recoverable.
proves: NVIDIA engineer: all asynchronous errors (e.g. illegal address) are sticky; the only recovery is letting the owning process terminate.
does_not_prove: Forum answer, not formal docs; does not cover MPS/green contexts or separate-process drafters.
bearing: C4: in-process drafter containment impossible for IMA-class faults; requires a separate process or restart
